text:
mira: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands. Can someone clarify the autoscaler "staggering" behavior you mentioned for regional burst? Specifically: how do we pick which regions to drain/burst first, and is there a guardrail to avoid cross-region thrash?

alex: Good Q. The short version: policy is priority -> capacity signal -> latency SLO. For a single customer request we attempt local region, then same-continent fallback, then global. Staggering = we open burst capacity in a weighted sequence to avoid doing all regions at once. :gear:

mira: When you say "weighted sequence", is that dynamic per-customer or static per-region?

alex: It's dynamic. Weight calc factors: historical demand (1h window), available idle GPUs, and contract tier. Rough pseudo: 
```
weights[r] = 0.6*demand_norm + 0.3*idle_capacity_norm + 0.1*tier_score
choose top-k regions until request_sla_met
```

devon: Will that affect dedicated customers? We promised isolation for Dedicated pools — won't burst for them.

alex: Correct — Dedicated pools are excluded from cross-customer bursting. The weights only apply to shared capacity (hosted). Dedicated has its own autoscaler config and can opt into regional spill only if the customer flips "allow_spill": true.

leo: Any ETA on shipping the public config docs for this? Folks on support need to explain fallbacks to customers.

alex: We're drafting the docs now. Goal: PR + internal explainer by next Tue, public docs by end of month. I'll ping the docs channel when the PR is up.

anna: Two quick ops checks: 1) what's the threshold to trigger global fallback (like when all local queues > X ms)? 2) will we signal clients with a header when fallback happens?

alex: 1) threshold is queue_length_avg > 200ms or token_throughput drop > 30% sustained for 2 minutes. 2) Yes — we emit `x-redwood-fallback-region` and `x-redwood-fallback-reason` on proxied responses for hosted customers. For private deployments that's opt-in.

devon: Any cost estimates for a typical APAC spike (say 2x traffic for 30m) if we trigger global burst vs. local-scale-up?

alex: Quick back-of-envelope: local-scale-up (on-demand regional GPUs) ~1.8x per-token cost due to spot premium and smaller batches; global-burst (using underutilized EU/US shared pools) tends to be ~1.2x because of better batching and larger instance types. But network egress and latency penalties apply. We'll provide the numbers in the docs + a sample calculator.

sre-bot: Incident note: we observed a transient spike in EU idle signal at 2026-02-12T11:03Z that triggered an early burst in canary. No customer impact. Logged under INC-2026-214.

mira: Awesome, thanks. Alex — can you add the policy YAML snippet to the PR so PMs/support can reference? Also, Leo, please coordinate a short FAQ for APAC customers on expected behavior.

alex: Will do.

leo: On it. I'll draft the FAQ and share tomorrow. :+1:

mira: Perfect — closing loop here. If anyone sees odd cross-region traffic overnight, ping infra pager and drop notes in #eng-sre. Thanks.
